newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end higher in line with soybean.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end higher in line with soybean.

text.p: All contracts of Tokyo corn futures closed higher on Friday, after fluctuating in a narrow range throughout the day amid a lack of major market factors, local traders said.
Prices were 10 to 80 yen higher, with the benchmark November 1997 contract up 20 yen at 14,160 yen per tonne. Daily volume was 25,376 lots.

Mostly contracts were weaker at the opening, reflecting the yen's firmness against the dollar, traders said. But the price gains of the yen-based Tokyo soybean futures market encouraged individual investors to build long positions later, they said.
The spot December contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $2.71 per bushel at 0750 GMT, compared with Thursday's closing price of $2.71-1/4.
The spot November contract of the CBOT soybean futures on the overnight trading system was at $6.91-1/4 at 0750 GMT, unchanged from Thursday's closing price.
